subject: HydraHealth SLA credit request — incident RI-20261101
messages:
From: Devon Patel <devon@hydrahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@hydrahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: SLA credit after Nov 1 outage - HydraHealth

Hi Soojin,

We experienced a significant availability event on 2026-11-01 (internal incident RI-20261101) that impacted our API traffic between 08:32–09:05 PT. Our platform saw ~40% request failures for ~33 minutes during peak. That caused degraded customer experiences for multiple internal teams at HydraHealth.

Per the Redwood SLA, we believe HydraHealth is eligible for a service credit for November usage. Can you confirm eligibility and provide the calculation and evidence package (uptime metrics, request logs, remediation notes)? Procurement would like a formal credit memo and any required signature/acceptance steps.

Attaching: request-logs.zip (request-level logs we captured).

Thanks,
Devon Patel
Head of Platform Ops, HydraHealth
devon@hydrahealth.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Patel <devon@hydrahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA credit after Nov 1 outage - HydraHealth

Hi Devon — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. I’m sorry for the disruption. We’re pulling together the incident timeline and eligibility calc now.

Next steps:
- I’ll coordinate the evidence package (uptime metrics, request-level sample, incident timeline).
- Ben, can you run the credit eligibility and prepare a draft credit memo (attach calc + XLS)?
- Marissa, can you advise on approval path — do we need Finance sign-off + legal acceptance for HydraHealth?

We expect to have a draft to share within 72 hours. If you have an SLA clause reference you want us to use for the calculation, paste it here; otherwise we’ll use the standard monthly credit formula in Section 4.2 of the agreement.

Soojin
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: SLA credit after Nov 1 outage - HydraHealth

Soojin / Marissa — attaching the calculation and raw metrics. Summary below and workbook is attached (credit-calculation.xlsx).

Summary of eligibility and calculation:
- Measured window: 2026-11-01 08:00–10:00 PT (we used RPS and 5xx/error-rate to determine impact window).
- Observed availability during billing period (Nov): 99.856% (after excluding scheduled maint windows).
- SLA target: 99.95% monthly availability.
- Shortfall: 0.094% of monthly availability => credit = shortfall * monthly invoice cap.
- HydraHealth’s committed monthly usage (invoice used for calc): $13,120.
- Calculated credit: 0.00094 * $13,120 = $12.33 (rounding rule per SLA = minimum $10? see note).

Notes:
- Because the incident duration is short and the overall monthly impact is below 1%, the dollar amount is small. Cortex billing rules call for rounding to the nearest dollar and a minimum credit floor of $10 for verified incidents.
- Evidence attached: uptime-metrics.csv (aggregated sample), incident-timeline.pdf (root-cause and mitigation notes), credit-calculation.xlsx (workbook with formulas).

Approval requested: Marissa, please confirm sign-off so we can issue a credit note and send the memo + DocuSign link to HydraHealth.

Ben
Senior Sales Engineer
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-04T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: SLA credit after Nov 1 outage - HydraHealth

Thanks Ben — I reviewed the calc and evidence. Given the contract language and rounding policy, approve issuing the credit. Action items:
- Finance: issue $12 credit to HydraHealth's Nov invoice (note: our internal minimum credit floor applied).
- Legal: no special exceptions required; standard credit memo and acceptance link is sufficient.
- Soojin: please send the credit memo to Devon and include DocuSign link for their acceptance.

I’m attaching the standard credit memo template and the signed incident timeline we will include with the customer package.

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Patel <devon@hydrahealth.com>
Cc: procure@hydrahealth.com, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Credit issued: HydraHealth — Incident RI-20261101

Hi Devon,

Thanks for your patience — we completed our review and have issued a service credit related to RI-20261101. Details below:

What we did:
- Investigated incident and validated impact window (2026-11-01 08:32–09:05 PT). Attached is the incident timeline (incident-timeline.pdf) and aggregated request metrics (uptime-metrics.csv).
- Applied contractual SLA formula and our rounding/minimum credit policy.

Credit details:
- Calculated credit: $12 (applied to HydraHealth Nov invoice).
- Credit memo: attached and available for acceptance here: https://redwood.app/docusign/HYDRA-CREDIT-2026
- Reference: Incident RI-20261101; Deal: HYDRA-PS-2026.

Attachments: incident-timeline.pdf, uptime-metrics.csv, credit-calculation.xlsx (detailed workbook).

Next steps for HydraHealth:
1) Review and accept the credit memo via the DocuSign link above (no signature required for small credits but acceptance gives us auditability).
2) If you prefer a one-off invoice adjustment instead of an applied credit, let me know by reply and I’ll loop in Finance.

If you have any questions about the calculation or need additional logs from our side, I can escalate a request to our Reliability team.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’ve implemented a hotfix to prevent recurrence in the same subsystem and will monitor closely.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
